standard_prerequisites: partial computable functions and their indices cf_e
the characteristic function of a set
Kleene's T predicate and unbounded minimization
enumerability as the domain of a partial computable function
core_obligations: Prove that the self-halting set K = {e : cf_e(e) is defined} is computably enumerable but not decidable
proof_roadmap: Suppose K decidable, so its characteristic function is computable; define the diagonal partial function d(e)=1 if the characteristic function of K vanishes at e, undefined otherwise
Let k be an index of d; then d(k) and cf_k(k) agree on definedness by definition of d, but d(k) is defined exactly when k is not in K, i.e. exactly when cf_k(k) is undefined -- contradiction
K is the domain of the partial computable function x maps to the least y with T(x,x,y), and domains of partial computable functions are computably enumerable
difficulty_reason: The undecidability half is the standard diagonal argument written out in full; the enumerability half is a one-line domain observation from the definition of c.e.
